newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end down, still in technical range.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end down, still in technical range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended lower Thursday in a sluggish session, but prices held in recent technical ranges, consolidating amid little reason to move far in either direction, industry sources said.
November slipped 0.9 cent to close at $2.428 per million British thermal units. December settled 2.5 cents lower at $2.595. Other deferreds ended steady to down two cents.

"ACCESS jumped (last night) on the AGAs, but we failed to follow through this morning. We're in a range here - buy the mid-$2.30s (basis November) and sell $2.50, but I think it's more likely we'll test the lower end," said one Midwest trader.

He said it would probably take a broad, sustained cold front to drive prices through resistance, something that is not predicted by forecasters just yet though the Midwest and Northeast are supposed to be chilly this weekend.
While Hurricane Lili may threaten Florida, most expected it to steer clear of U.S. Gulf production.
At 1400 EDT, Lili was about 185 miles south-southwest of Havana, Cuba, packing winds of 75 mph, moving north-northeast at nine mph. The storm was expected to hit Cuba late Thursday or early Friday.
Technically, traders agreed recent ranges were intact, with support and resistance in November still in the mid-$2.30s and the $2.51 area (double top), respectively.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast cash prices were little changed Thursday in the mid-$2.30s, more than 50 cents over October indices. Prospects for colder Midcontinent weather firmed pipes there by a few cents to the low-$2.30s, 60 cents over October 1 levels.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip eased 1.5 cents to $2.205. NYMEX said 24,812 Hub contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 39,537.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled one-half cent lower at $1.07, while most deferreds closed unchanged. NYMEX said 22 Alberta contracts traded, down from Wednesday's total of 23.

NYMEX November Permian natgas finished four cents higher at $2.18, while deferreds settled up by four to nine cents but were untraded. NYMEX said three Permian lots changed hands versus no trading on Wednesday.

On KCBT, November closed 2.5 cents higher at $2.235, while deferreds ended up by one-half to 1.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 3.4 cents to 19.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 599 contracts traded, up from Wednesday's total of 501.
